answer: On a still night the grass temperature falls several degrees below the air temperature, and the claimant reports both at the coldest hour, verified against the station's own divergence. A zephyr too weak to stir the air lets the ground cool fastest, a signal from the sensor confirms the gap, and a canyon floor freezes while the rim above stays warmer. One warm room cannot produce fifty different ground-air gaps, because each gap depends on the real sky, soil and wind of its own field.
